facts.statement: Bravoceratops was a large chasmosaurine ceratopsid that lived about 70 million years ago in the Late Cretaceous Javelina Formation of present-day Texas.
facts.quote: Bravoceratops is a genus of large chasmosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur that lived approximately 70 million years ago, and is known from the Late Cretaceous Javelina Formation in what is now Texas, United States.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Bravoceratops is holotype TxVP 46015-1, which is housed in the Texas Vertebrate Paleontology Collections in Austin.
facts.quote: Bravoceratops is only known from the holotype specimen TxVP 46015-1; it is housed in the Texas Vertebrate Paleontology Collections, Austin, Texas.

facts.statement: Bravoceratops was named by Steven L. Wick and Thomas M. Lehman in 2013.
facts.quote: The genus was described and named by Steven L. Wick and Thomas M. Lehman in 2013

facts.statement: The skull fossil includes fragments of the braincase, brow horns, postorbital, nasal area, jugals, quadrates, parietal, epiparietals, dentary, and squamosal.
facts.quote: The skull consists of a number of fragments, altogether including: the braincase, parts of each brow horn, the rear end of the left postorbital, assorted parts of the nasal area and horn, the jugals, quadrates and quadratojugals from each side, a section of the parietal and epiparietals, multiple parts of the dentary, and some of the right squamosal.

facts.statement: The genus name Bravoceratops means "wild horn-face", combining the Mexican name Rio Bravo del Norte with Greek words for horn and face.
facts.quote: The genus name means "wild horn-face", and is derived from the Mexican name for the Rio Grande, "Rio Bravo del Norte" (wild river of the north), and the Greek words "keras" (κέρας) meaning "horn" and "ops" (ὤψ) referring to the "face".

facts.statement: The specific name references a hollow in the parietal bar shaped like an inverted tear, resembling the single eye of the cyclops Polyphemus.
facts.quote: It is this hollow in the form of an inverted tear that occasioned the specific name as it resembled the single eye of a cyclops, thus the allusion with Polyphemus.

facts.statement: In 2020, Fowler and Freedman Fowler suggested the genus was invalid because the parietal bar was likely reconstructed upside down, removing its distinguishing features.
facts.quote: In 2020, paleontologists Denver W. Fowler and Elizabeth A. Freedman Fowler suggested that the parietal median bar of the specimen had been reconstructed upside down, and that the genus therefore did not have any distinguishing features among chasmosaurines, making it a nomen dubium, or invalid genus.

facts.statement: Bravoceratops has a large flange in front of the quadrate near the jugal bones, a trait shared with Sierraceratops but rare in other chasmosaurs.
facts.quote: A flange in front of its quadrate near the jugal bones is present, large as in Sierraceratops while small or not present in other chasmosaurs.

facts.statement: Bravoceratops has compressed brow horns that are taller than wide, a trait shared with Sierraceratops and Judiceratops.
facts.quote: The two brow horns are compressed, being taller than wide rather than conical, a trait shared with Sierraceratops and the distantly related Judiceratops.

facts.statement: Bravoceratops is classified within the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Bravoceratops is assigned to the Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: Bravoceratops is an intermediate chasmosaurine, more advanced than Chasmosaurus but less so than Triceratops.
facts.quote: It is an "intermediate" form of chasmosaurine; it, along with genera like Pentaceratops and Anchiceratops, was distinctly more derived ("advanced") than forms like Chasmosaurus but less so than taxa like Triceratops.

facts.statement: Bravoceratops is considered the sister taxon of Coahuilaceratops, a relationship supported by Dalman et al. in 2021.
facts.quote: It was found that Bravoceratops may be the sister taxon of Coahuilaceratops (a relationship later supported by Dalman et al., 2021).

facts.statement: Due to its fragmentary nature, Bravoceratops is often excluded from phylogenetic analyses as it acts as an unstable wildcard taxon.
facts.quote: However, the fragmentary nature of Bravoceratops caused it to generally be removed from phylogenetic analyses, as it was a wildcard taxon (meaning it was unstable and caused poorer results).

facts.statement: Bravoceratops is part of a clade endemic to the Southwestern United States, alongside Coahuilaceratops and Sierraceratops.
facts.quote: As a result, Bravoceratops was determined to be part of a clade endemic to the Southwestern United States, including Coahuilaceratops from Mexico and Sierraceratops from New Mexico.

facts.statement: The discovery is significant because ceratopsian fossils are found only rarely in the Javelina Formation.
facts.quote: Este descubrimiento es significativo porque paleontológicamente restos de dinosaurios ceratopsianos ocurren sólo raramente en la formación Javelina

facts.statement: Bravoceratops displays a distinctive combination of traits not seen in any previously described chasmosaurine.
facts.quote: Bravoceratops muestra una distintiva combinación de rasgos no vistos en ningún casmosaurino anteriormente descrito.

facts.statement: Bravoceratops was among the largest chasmosaurines.
facts.quote: Bravoceratops estuvo entre los mayores casmosaurinos.

facts.statement: The size of the occipital condyle is comparable to that of other large chasmosaurines such as Torosaurus and Triceratops.
facts.quote: El tamaño del cóndilo occipital es comparable al de otros casmosaurinos grandes tales como Torosaurus y Triceratops.

facts.statement: It had a distinctive narrow snout, a large frill formed by the squamosal and parietal bones with large elongated openings, large robust epijugal "horns", long horns over the brow, and a bifurcated squatoyugal-squamosal contact.
facts.quote: Tenía un distintivo hocico estrecho, una gran gola formada por los huesos escamosal y parietal con grandes aberturas alargadas, "cuernos" epiyugales grandes y robustos, largos cuernos sobre la frente y un contacto cuadratoyugal-escamosal bifurcado.

facts.statement: It was found in the strata of the Javelina Formation in Big Bend National Park in Texas, USA.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en los estratos de la formación Javelina en el parque nacional Big Bend en el estado de Texas (EE. UU.).

facts.statement: The genus was named and described by Steven L. Wick and Thomas M. Lehman in 2013.
facts.quote: Bravoceratops fue nombrado y descrito por Steven L. Wick y Thomas M. Lehman en 2013

facts.statement: The genus name Bravoceratops means "horned face of the Rio Bravo", derived from the Rio Grande and Greek words for horn and face.
facts.quote: El nombre de género Bravoceratops significa "cara con cuernos del río Bravo", derivado del nombre del río Bravo del Norte, también conocido como el río Grande en Estados Unidos,y las palabras griegas "keras" (κέρας) que significa "cuerno" y "ops" (ὤψ) que se traduce como "cara"

facts.statement: The species name polyphemus refers to the giant cyclops Polyphemus confronted by Odysseus in the Greek epic the Odyssey.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie polyphemus, se refiere al cíclope gigante Polifemo que fue confrontado por Odiseo en la clásica epopeya griega la Odisea.

facts.statement: The species is known from the holotype specimen TMM 46015-1, which consists of a fragmentary skull in good preservation providing adequate diagnostic data.
facts.quote: Esta especie es conocida a partir del espécimen holotipo TMM 46015-1, el cual consiste de un cráneo fragmentario en buen estado de preservación que provee datos de diagnóstico adecuados.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is housed in the collection of the Texas Memorial Museum in Austin, Texas.
facts.quote: Este espécimen es alojado en la colección del Texas Memorial Museum en Austin (Texas).

facts.statement: The various parts of the holotype skull were completely disarticulated and scattered over an area of approximately ten square meters before fossilization.
facts.quote: La varias partes del cráneo del holotipo estaban completamente desarticuladas y esparcidas por un área de aproximadamente diez metros cuadrados antes de su fosilización.

facts.statement: Many of the more robust remains, such as the horns, exhibit erosion and wear, suggesting the skull remained exposed for a time before being buried.
facts.quote: Muchos de los restos más robustos, como los cuernos, exhiben erosión y desgaste. Esta circunstancia sugiere que el cráneo permaneció expuesto por un tiempo antes de quedar enterrado.

facts.statement: The specimen was collected from a conglomerate of sandstone sediments deposited at the beginning of the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue recolectado en un conglomerado de sedimentos de areniscas que fue depositado a principios de la etapa del Maastrichtiense, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años.

facts.statement: Studies suggest the paleoenvironment of this section of the Javelina Formation was a river plain located several hundred kilometers inland, far from the nearest coastline.
facts.quote: Los estudios sugieren que el paleoambiente de esta sección de la Formación Javelina era una planicie fluvial que se encontraba a varios cientos de kilómetros tierra adentro, lejos de la línea costera más cercana.

facts.statement: Bravoceratops was assigned to the subfamily Chasmosaurinae in 2013.
facts.quote: Bravoceratops fue asignado en 2013 a la subfamilia Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: Analysis suggested Bravoceratops may be the sister species of Coahuilaceratops, though this relationship is poorly supported due to few available elements for direct comparison.
facts.quote: El análisis sugirió que Bravoceratops puede ser la especie hermana de Coahuilaceratops, aunque esta relación no está bien soprotada ya que hay muy pocos elementos disponibles para hacer una comparación directa de estos dos géneros.

facts.statement: The presence of a midline epiparietal on the distal margin of the frill and the bifurcated squatoyugal–squamosal articulation in the skull are considered derived traits.
facts.quote: La presencia de un epiparietal en la línea media en el margen distal de la gola, y la articulación bifurcada cuadratoyugal–escamosal en el cráneo, son considerados como rasgos derivados.

facts.statement: The time range is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: It belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: It belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
